openbao.description: How a process reaches an OpenBAO transit engine: where it is, and exactly one way of signing in.

caFile.description: A PEM bundle trusted beside the system roots, for a server on a private chain.

login.description: Sign in with a JWT: the pod's projected service-account token, presented to an auth mount. Nothing is stored.

jwtFile.description: The file holding the JWT, read at every login because the kubelet replaces a projected token before it expires.

mount.description: The JWT auth mount, for example jwt-devel.
Where the transit engine is mounted.

namespace.description: The OpenBAO namespace the engine and the auth mount are in. Unset is the root namespace.

tokenEnv.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding a token.

tokenFile.description: A file holding a token, read on every call, for a token something else keeps renewed.

sink.description: The writer this process records through.

expect.description: What the writer at `url` is configured to give: `archived` for a writer, `queued` for a receiver in front of a queue, `logged` for one that only logs. A client cannot learn it until it writes, so the file says, and `require` is checked against it at start-up and against every acknowledgement afterwards.

tokenFile.description: A file holding the token presented to the writer, read afresh on every request: in a cluster, the pod's projected service-account token. Unset presents none, which an anonymous trial install accepts.

description: The configuration of `audit digest --config`, which seals windows into the signed chain. Secrets are never in this file: a field named ...Env holds the NAME of the environment variable that holds the secret. Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

archive.description: Where the archive is and how it is written.

lockMode.description: The Object Lock mode every object is written in: compliance (the record tier), governance (a lock a privileged role can shorten), or none (the attested tier, for a store without Object Lock). A process refuses to start when a profile demands a stricter mode than this.

prefix.description: The prefix within the bucket. Required in a bucket shared with other installations: it is what keeps two of them apart.

lookback.description: How far before a window to look for objects keyed under an older day. The verify job's must be at least this.

maxWindows.description: How many windows one run may seal when catching up.

require.description: The weakest durability an acknowledgement from the writer may carry (`logged`, `queued` or `archived`). Unset checks nothing. Set, it needs `sink.expect` at least as strong, which is checked at start-up, and an acknowledgement weaker than this fails the write instead of passing it with a caveat. See ADR 0017.

signer.description: What the digests are signed with: exactly one. An unsigned chain proves nothing, and one chain has one signer.

id.description: The name a digest records the signing key under.

kmsKey.description: An AWS KMS ECC_NIST_P256 key. The private half never leaves KMS.

transit.description: An OpenBAO transit ed25519 key, signed in to as the job's own identity and never the writer's.

sink.description: The writer this job records what it sealed through (audit.digest.written).

title: audit digest
